title: The text discusses the significant impact of the HIV/AIDS pandemic on life expectancy in Africa, highlighting that many African countries have life expectancies below 50 years, in stark contrast to other developing nations. The World Health Organization (WHO) has introduced a new metric called Disability Adjusted Life Expectancy (DALE), which measures healthy life expectancy by accounting for years lived with disabilities. Japan ranks highest with a healthy life expectancy of 74.5 years, while Sierra Leone ranks lowest at less than 26 years. The United States ranks 24th with an average of 70 years, revealing disparities in health outcomes among different demographics, particularly among marginalized groups. The text emphasizes the need to address health inequalities and the effects of diseases like HIV/AIDS and tobacco-related illnesses on life expectancy.
